stages.headline: P(cos α; sin α) lies on x² + y² = 1, so sin²α + cos²α = 1 for every α.
stages.headlineEnglish: P(cos α; sin α) lies on x² + y² = 1, so sin²α + cos²α = 1 for every α.

stages.headline: Other identities: tg α · ctg α = 1, 1 + tg²α = 1/cos²α, 1 + ctg²α = 1/sin²α.
stages.headlineEnglish: Other identities: tg α · ctg α = 1, 1 + tg²α = 1/cos²α, 1 + ctg²α = 1/sin²α.

stages.headline: Example: sin α = 3/5, α ∈ (π/2; π): cos α = −4/5 (quadrant II), tg α = −3/4, ctg α = −4/3.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: sin α = 3/5, α ∈ (π/2; π): cos α = −4/5 (quadrant II), tg α = −3/4, ctg α = −4/3.
